intro: What people are saying about GTA 6 that Rockstar hasn't confirmed. Each claim has a status, what would settle it and where it came from. We check them against the real game after launch and move them to Confirmed or Debunked.

statuses.rumour: Rumour: a claim from an insider or leaker, nothing official
statuses.leak: Leak: material that appeared without Rockstar's approval; not fully verified
statuses.reported: Reported: covered by established outlets citing sources, not confirmed by Rockstar
statuses.estimate: Estimate: community measurement or maths, not an official figure
statuses.confirmed: Confirmed: Rockstar or the game itself shows it's true

items.title: GTA 6 Online arrives within weeks of launch
items.summary: Rockstar hasn't announced the online mode, and it isn't part of the 19 November launch. A leaker known as TheGhostOfHope claimed it would follow within about a month, before Christmas. Data miners say multiplayer code is already in the release build. On the other side, Bloomberg's Jason Schreier hasn't expected an announcement soon, and a mix-up over a Bloomberg remark briefly spread a 2027 date that wasn't actually reported.
items.settles: An announcement from Rockstar, or an online mode appearing in the game's menus.

items.title: About 17 million copies sold on day one
items.summary: Analytics firm Sensor Tower estimates GTA 6 sold more than 17 million copies, worth over $1.65 billion, by early on launch day, which would be well past GTA V's first-day revenue. Take-Two and Rockstar haven't published any sales figures yet.
items.settles: Official numbers from Take-Two, most likely in a press release or its next earnings report.

sources.title: Reuters via Dawn: Sensor Tower estimate and launch reaction
Happy Gamer: the figure is not an official number

items.title: Story DLC with new cities and missions
items.summary: Insider Tez2 said in 2022 that Rockstar is returning to single-player expansions, with new cities and missions planned before launch, the way GTA IV got The Lost and Damned. GTA V never got story DLC. Rockstar hasn't said anything about post-launch story content.
items.settles: Rockstar announcing an expansion, or areas of the map that are clearly closed off for later.

sources.title: GamesRadar: GTA 6 will reportedly go back to single-player DLC
GameSpot: rumour suggests a return to single-player DLC

items.title: Leonida has five counties: Vice Dale, Mariana, Kelly, Leonard and Lummox
items.summary: The in-game map of the released game splits Leonida into the same five counties the August leak showed: Vice-Dale, Mariana, Kelly, Leonard and Lummox. Before launch, the printed map in the Collector's Edition, put on display at Selfridges in Manchester, had already shown Lummox County, the one name nobody had seen before the leak.
items.settles: Settled: the in-game map shows all five counties.

items.title: How much bigger the map is than GTA V's
items.summary: Rockstar still hasn't given a size. Before launch, fans measuring the leaked map mostly landed between 1.5 and 3 times GTA V's land, with about 125 square kilometres the most cited figure against GTA V's 48. The first measurement of the released game's map puts the whole play area at about 175 square kilometres (roughly 16 by 11 km), around 65% of it land. That works out to about 114 square kilometres of land, a little under two and a half times GTA V's.
items.settles: More measurements from the released game agreeing, or an official figure from Rockstar.

items.title: Vehicles need refuelling, and police notice what you're wearing
items.summary: Both ideas first surfaced in the August leak and now hold up. Refuelling was shown at Rockstar's own preview at Rockstar North: gas stations let you refuel, charge an electric car or repair, with a short animation of about 10 seconds, and the studio's co-head commented on it. Reviews of the finished game say witnesses, cameras and your clothes or car all affect how police look for you. The leak's third claim, picking weapons from a loadout, only partly held: Bloomberg's Jason Schreier reported that the final game uses a weapon wheel again, though outlets report a limit on how many guns you carry.
items.settles: Settled for refuelling and police: Rockstar showed refuelling at its preview, and reviewers saw the police behaviour in the finished game.

items.title: The PC version comes in early 2027
items.summary: GamesBeat reported that GTA 6 reaches PC in the first quarter of 2027, much sooner than GTA V's 19-month gap. Rockstar hasn't announced a PC version or commented.
items.settles: A Rockstar announcement or a store page.

sources.title: Dexerto: GamesBeat report on the PC version
PCWorld: Rockstar did not comment

items.title: Another delay to 2027
items.summary: Delay claims went viral several times in 2026, often from misread comments. The game kept its date: pre-orders opened in June, pre-loading started on 10 November, and it launched on 19 November.
